mainTopic: How to read the משנה of תם and מועד, crouching on vessels, and identifying the ברדלס
overview: The גמרא first tries to say the whole משנה follows רבי טרפון. It does this by explaining one line as a shared courtyard, which counts as the injured party's courtyard for שן but as public property for קרן. רב זביד rejects this, because רבי טרפון would make even unusual eating pay in full. So the גמרא reads the משנה as following the רבנן, with missing words filled in. רבינא objects using a later משנה and gives his own fuller reading: five acts start as תם and can become מועד; שן ורגל are always מועד; damage on the injured party's property is a מחלוקת between רבי טרפון and the רבנן; and certain wild animals are also מועד. A ברייתא matches his reading exactly. Next, רבי אלעזר discusses whether crouching on small vessels counts as normal behavior, and the גמרא gives several versions of that discussion. Finally, the גמרא identifies the ברדלס as the female hyena and the צבוע of רבי מאיר as the male. It then starts to look again at רבי מאיר's addition.

steps.title: The whole משנה follows רבי טרפון, using a shared courtyard
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proposes that the entire משנה follows רבי טרפון. It explains a problem line as a case of a jointly owned courtyard with split usage rights.
steps.simpleTranslation: The whole משנה is רבי טרפון. The earlier line is about a courtyard shared by two partners. Only one of them may keep produce there, but both may keep oxen there. So for eating (שן) it counts as the injured party's courtyard. For goring (קרן) it counts like a public domain.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers an answer: the whole משנה can follow רבי טרפון. It sets the troublesome line in a special shared courtyard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same courtyard is treated differently depending on the type of damage. The produce belongs there only for the injured partner, so eating it is like damage in his own courtyard and is paid in full. Both partners may keep oxen there, so for goring it is like public property, and an ox that is a תם pays half.

keyTerms.meaning: The whole of it (the entire משנה)
The first part of a statement or clause
A courtyard designated for a specific use

steps.confusionAlert: The courtyard is not simply 'private' or 'public'. It gets a different status for each type of damage, because the partners agreed to different uses.

phrases.english: The whole [משנה] is Rabbi Tarfon;

phrases.aramaic: רֵישָׁא – בְּחָצֵר הַמְיוּחֶדֶת לְפֵירוֹת לְאֶחָד מֵהֶן,
phrases.english: the first part is in a courtyard designated for produce for one of them,
and for this one and that one for oxen;

phrases.aramaic: דִּלְגַבֵּי שֵׁן הָוְיָא לַהּ חֲצַר הַנִּיזָּק.
phrases.english: so regarding Tooth, it is the injured party's courtyard.
And regarding Horn, it is a public domain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the earlier question about whose view the משנה follows
steps.terutzResolutionType: Recasting the case (אוקימתא) as a shared courtyard with split rights
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The line seemed to treat the courtyard as public, which would go against רבי טרפון
steps.terutzMaskana: For שן it is the injured party's courtyard; for קרן it is public, so the whole משנה fits רבי טרפון

steps.title: רב זביד objects using the line about fitting food
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא reports that רב זביד challenged this answer. The משנה says the tooth is מועד only for food fitting for the animal, which implies unfitting food is not paid in full.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: I told this teaching to רב זביד of נהרדעא, and he said to me: Can you really say the whole משנה is רבי טרפון? The משנה teaches, 'The tooth is מועד to eat what is fitting for it.' Fitting food is paid in full. Food that is not fitting is not.
steps.whatsHappening: רב זביד starts a challenge. He points to a line in the משנה and draws an inference from it. The next step will show why this inference clashes with רבי טרפון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'what is fitting for it' imply a contrast: eating unfitting food is not treated as normal eating. So the owner would not pay full damage, even though שן only applies in the injured party's courtyard.

keyTerms.meaning: Are you able to set (interpret) it
Forewarned: its owner pays full damage

phrases.english: Rav Kahana said:

phrases.aramaic: אַמְרִיתַהּ לִשְׁמַעְתָּא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב זְבִיד מִנְּהַרְדְּעָא,
phrases.english: I said this teaching before Rav Zevid of Neharde'a,
and he said to me:

phrases.aramaic: מִי מָצֵית מוֹקְמַתְּ לַהּ כּוּלַּהּ כְּרַבִּי טַרְפוֹן?!
phrases.english: Can you really set the whole of it like Rabbi Tarfon?!

phrases.aramaic: הָקָתָנֵי: ״הַשֵּׁן מוּעֶדֶת לֶאֱכוֹל אֶת הָרָאוּי לָהּ״;
phrases.english: But it teaches: "The tooth is forewarned to eat what is fitting for it";
fitting for it, yes;
what is not fitting for it, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי מָצֵית מוֹקְמַתְּ לַהּ כּוּלַּהּ כְּרַבִּי טַרְפוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer that the whole משנה is רבי טרפון
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the entire משנה follows רבי טרפון
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An inference from the משנה: eating unfitting food is not paid in full

steps.title: רבי טרפון would require full payment
steps.stepSummary: רב זביד completes the challenge. רבי טרפון holds that even unusual damage in the injured party's courtyard is paid in full, so he would not reduce payment for unfitting food.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the משנה were רבי טרפון, there is a problem: he says that unusual damage like goring, done in the injured party's courtyard, is paid in full!
steps.whatsHappening: This finishes רב זביד's challenge. רבי טרפון's own rule contradicts what the משנה implied.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Eating unfitting food is unusual behavior, just like goring (קרן). רבי טרפון says unusual damage in the injured party's courtyard is paid in full. So according to him, there is no reason to limit full payment to fitting food. The משנה's wording therefore cannot be רבי טרפון.

keyTerms.meaning: Horn: goring and similar intentional damage

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's words 'what is fitting for it' cannot fit רבי טרפון. He makes unusual damage in the injured party's courtyard pay in full.

phrases.english: And if it is Rabbi Tarfon, doesn't he say:
unusual damage, Horn, in the injured party's courtyard,
he pays full damage!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge begun in the previous step
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the whole משנה is רבי טרפון
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי טרפון's rule (unusual damage in the injured party's courtyard is paid in full) contradicts the משנה's implied rule

steps.title: The משנה follows the רבנן, with missing words
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops the רבי טרפון approach. It says the משנה follows the רבנן and reads its opening as one list: the same five acts start as תם and can become מועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the משנה really follows the רבנן. Some words are missing, and this is what it means: there are five acts that are תם, and if the animal was warned, all five become מועד.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new answer: the משנה follows the רבנן. Its opening line is not two separate lists but one list that can change status.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's opening, 'five are תם and five are מועד', is no longer read as ten different acts. It describes the same five goring-type acts. They start as תם and become מועד after warnings. With the משנה following the רבנן, the line about 'fitting' food no longer causes a problem.

keyTerms.meaning: The text is missing words that must be read in
Innocent: the owner pays half damage

steps.whatToRemember: New approach: the משנה follows the רבנן and is missing words. Read its opening as 'five are תם, and if warned, those same five become מועד'. The next step finishes this reading, and רבינא challenges it in step 6.
steps.whyThisMatters: This changes how we read the very first line of the פרק: one set of five acts, not two separate lists.

phrases.english: Rather, it really is the Rabbis;
and it is missing words, and this is what it teaches:
five are innocent,
and if they were warned, all five of them are forewarned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Abandons the רבי טרפון approach after the challenge and offers a new reading
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading missing words into the משנה (חסורי מחסרא) and assigning it to the רבנן
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The whole משנה follows רבי טרפון
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה follows the רבנן; the same five acts start as תם and can become מועד

steps.title: Finishing the reading: tooth and foot are forewarned, but only in the injured party's courtyard
steps.stepSummary: The reading from step 4 is completed. שן ורגל are מועד from the start, and 'בחצר הניזק' tells us where that status applies.
steps.simpleTranslation: And Tooth and Foot are forewarned from the very start. And where does that forewarned status apply? In the courtyard of the injured party.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps reading the משנה the way step 4 set it up. It turns the words 'בחצר הניזק' into the answer to a question: where are שן ורגל forewarned?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this reading, 'בחצר הניזק' is not a new case about goring. It only explains שן ורגל, which are liable only on the injured party's property. That way the משנה says nothing about goring in the injured party's courtyard, so it can fit the רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Tooth' — damage an animal does by eating
'Foot' — damage an animal does by trampling as it walks
Forewarned from the start, with full payment even the first time
The courtyard or property of the injured party

phrases.english: And Tooth and Foot are forewarned from their start.
And where is their forewarned status?
phrases.notes: In this reading, the משנה's words are read as a question and answer about שן ורגל.

phrases.english: In the courtyard of the injured party.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the reading of the משנה that step 4 began.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'בחצר הניזק' looked like a separate case about goring on the injured party's property, which would follow רבי טרפון.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'בחצר הניזק' only says where שן ורגל are forewarned, so the משנה can follow the רבנן.

steps.title: רבינא: a later משנה shows ours was talking about goring
steps.stepSummary: רבינא points to a later משנה that asks 'how so?' about an ox damaging on the injured party's property and then discusses goring. That only makes sense if our משנה listed that case.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא challenged this: The משנה later on teaches, 'An ox that does damage on the property of the injured party — how so?' If you say our משנה deals with that case, that is why the later one asks 'how so?' But if you say our משנה does not deal with it, what is that 'how so?' asking about?
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא attacks the reading in step 5. He uses a later משנה to show that our משנה must have mentioned goring on the injured party's property as its own case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The later משנה opens with 'שור המזיק ברשות הניזק כיצד' and goes on to explain cases of goring. A 'how so?' explains something that was already said. If our משנה only meant שן ורגל, there would be nothing about goring there for the later משנה to explain.

keyTerms.meaning: He challenged it, attacking an explanation that was just given
Later on, further ahead in the text
How so? A word that opens an explanation of something already stated

phrases.english: Ravina challenged it:
But it teaches later on:
phrases.notes: This is a later משנה in the same פרק, on דף 24b.

phrases.english: 'An ox that damages on the property of the injured party — how so?'
It makes sense if you say [our משנה] deals with it,
because of that it teaches 'how so?'

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִי אָמְרַתְּ לָא אַיְירִי בַּהּ,
phrases.english: But if you say it does not deal with it,
what is the 'how so?'

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רָבִינָא, הָא קָתָנֵי לְקַמַּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading completed in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that 'בחצר הניזק' only explains where שן ורגל are forewarned.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The later משנה's 'כיצד' explains goring on the injured party's property. So our משנה must have stated that case, which the step 5 reading leaves out.

steps.title: רבינא: the משנה is missing words — five acts that can become forewarned
steps.stepSummary: רבינא says the משנה has missing words. He starts his own reading: five acts start as תם, and if they are warned, all five become מועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבינא said: The משנה is missing words, and this is what it teaches: There are five acts that are innocuous. And if the animal was warned about them, all five become forewarned.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the earlier reading failed, רבינא offers a new way to read the משנה by filling in missing words. This step gives the first part of his reading, and the next step finishes it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like step 4, רבינא reads the opening as one list: the same five acts start as תם and can become מועד. The new part comes next, where he treats 'שור המזיק ברשות הניזק' as its own case.

keyTerms.meaning: It is missing words, so we fill in the full meaning
And this is what it teaches
Innocuous animals or acts; the owner pays only half damages
They were warned, meaning the animal did it three times

phrases.english: Rather, Ravina said:
It is missing words,
and this is what it teaches:
There are five that are innocuous.
And if they were warned, all five of them are forewarned;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבינא's own challenge in step 6 by offering a new reading.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's opening list had to be read in a way that left out goring on the injured party's property.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה has missing words. Its first part is one list of five acts that start as תם and can become מועד.

steps.title: רבינא's reading finished: damage on the injured party's property is a dispute
steps.stepSummary: רבינא finishes his reading. שן ורגל are always מועד. An ox damaging on the injured party's property is a separate case that רבי טרפון and the רבנן argue about. Certain wild animals are also מועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: And Tooth and Foot are forewarned from the start; and this is the forewarned ox. And an ox that damages on the injured party's property is a dispute between רבי טרפון and the רבנן. And there are other forewarned ones like these: the wolf, the lion, the bear, the ברדלס, the leopard, and the snake.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא completes his new reading of the משנה. The key change is that 'an ox that damages on the injured party's property' is now its own case, a disagreement between רבי טרפון and the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the משנה now does mention this case, the later משנה's 'כיצד' has something to explain, so רבינא's challenge is answered. The משנה also no longer has to follow only רבי טרפון. It simply reports his מחלוקת with the רבנן about goring on the injured party's property, where רבי טרפון says full payment and the רבנן say half.

keyTerms.meaning: The forewarned ox, whose owner pays full damages
On the property of the injured party
A kind of wild beast of prey

steps.whatToRemember: In רבינא's final reading, the משנה is missing words. שן ורגל are always מועד. 'שור המזיק ברשות הניזק' is a separate case, a מחלוקת between רבי טרפון and the רבנן. This explains why the later משנה asks 'כיצד' about it.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up 'בחצר הניזק' in step 5 with 'ברשות הניזק' here. In step 5 the words only said where שן ורגל apply. In רבינא's reading, damage on the injured party's property is its own disputed case.
steps.whyThisMatters: This reading lets the משנה match the later משנה on 24b. It also avoids saying the whole משנה follows only one side.

phrases.english: And Tooth and Foot are forewarned from their start;
and this is the forewarned ox.
phrases.notes: He means everyone agrees about this one: שן ורגל are clearly the forewarned ox.

phrases.english: And an ox that damages on the property of the injured party —
is a dispute between רבי טרפון and the Rabbis.
phrases.notes: רבי טרפון's side was quoted in step 3: goring there is paid in full. The רבנן say half.

phrases.english: And there are other forewarned ones similar to these —
the wolf, the lion, the bear,
the bardelas, the leopard, and the snake.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְשׁוֹר הַמַּזִּיק בִּרְשׁוּת הַנִּיזָּק – מַחְלוֹקֶת רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן וְרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the reading רבינא began in step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Filling in missing words, which makes the disputed case a separate item
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'שור המזיק ברשות הניזק' had to be either רבי טרפון's ruling or just a detail about שן ורגל.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is a separate case that רבי טרפון and the רבנן argue about. That gives the later משנה's 'כיצד' something to explain.

steps.title: A ברייתא matches רבינא's reading
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא is quoted that teaches exactly what רבינא said the משנה means.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is also taught this way in a ברייתא: There are five that are תם, and if they were warned, all five are מועד. שן ורגל are מועד from the start, and this is 'the forewarned ox.' An ox damaging on the injured party's property is a dispute between רבי טרפון and the רבנן. And there are other מועדים like these: the wolf, the lion, the bear, the leopard, the ברדלס, and the snake.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that a ברייתא says, word for word, what רבינא claimed the משנה really means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In steps 7-8, רבינא said the משנה has missing words and filled them in. Here a ברייתא is found that has those 'missing' words written out in full. That makes his reading much stronger, because it is not just a guess.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way (in a ברייתא), which brings support
They were warned (the owner was told three times), so the animal becomes מועד
From the start, without any warnings needed

steps.whyThisMatters: It confirms רבינא's structure of the משנה. There are five acts that start as תם and can become מועד. There are שן ורגל, which are always מועד. There is the disputed case of the injured party's property. And there are the wild animals.

phrases.english: It is also taught this way:
There are five that are תם (innocuous).
And if they were warned, all five of them are מועד;
and Tooth and Foot are מועד from the start;
and this is 'the forewarned ox.'
And an ox that damages on the injured party's property —
is a dispute between Rabbi Tarfon and the Rabbis.
And there are other forewarned ones similar to these:
the wolf, and the lion, the bear,
and the leopard, and the bardelas, and the snake.
phrases.notes: A ברדלס is a kind of dangerous wild animal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings support from a ברייתא for רבינא's reading in steps 7-8.
steps.raayaObject: רבינא's claim that the משנה is missing words and should be read as he laid it out.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא whose wording matches רבינא's filled-in version of the משנה exactly.

steps.title: Another version: the משנה seems to contradict itself
steps.stepSummary: Some tell the discussion differently. In their version, the question is that the משנה says 'five מועדים' but then lists more animals that are also מועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: There are those who raise it as a contradiction: We learned, 'Five are תם and five are מועד.' And there are no more?! But there are also the wolf, the lion, the bear, the leopard, the ברדלס, and the snake!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of how this discussion started. In this version, the question comes from a contradiction inside our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version (step 6), רבינא's question came from a later משנה. Here the question is different. The משנה counts exactly five מועדים, yet it also names wild animals that are מועד. So how can the count be only five? This sets up the same answer from רבינא.

keyTerms.meaning: There are those who present it as a contradiction (another version of the discussion)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new question added on top of step 6. It is another way the same discussion was told, and it ends with the same answer from רבינא.

phrases.english: There are those who raise it as a contradiction:
We learned: Five are innocuous
and five are forewarned.
And there are no more?!
But there are the wolf, the lion, and the bear,
and the leopard, and the bardelas, and the snake!
phrases.notes: These animals are named later in the same משנה as being מועד.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second version of how the question in step 6 was asked.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's opening count: 'five תמים and five מועדים.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If there are only five מועדים, the wild animals the משנה itself lists as מועד make the count wrong.

steps.title: רבינא answers: the משנה is missing words
steps.stepSummary: In this version too, רבינא answers that the משנה has missing words. He gives the full reading, which lists the wild animals as a separate group.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they answer, as רבינא said: The משנה is missing words, and this is what it teaches: There are five that are תם, and if they were warned, all five are מועד. שן ורגל are מועד from the start, and this is 'the forewarned ox.' An ox damaging on the injured party's property is a dispute between רבי טרפון and the רבנן. And there are other מועדים like these: the wolf, the lion, the bear, the leopard, the ברדלס, and the snake.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction with רבינא's reading. The words are the same as before, now repeated to solve this second version of the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the missing words filled in, 'five מועדים' only means the five acts that become מועד after warnings. The wild animals are added at the end as a separate group, 'other מועדים like these.' So nothing contradicts, because the count of five was never meant to include them.

keyTerms.meaning: It is missing words (the משנה must be read with words filled in)
And this is what it teaches

steps.whatToRemember: Both versions of the question end the same way. רבינא reads the משנה as: five acts that become מועד after warnings, שן ורגל always מועד, the disputed case of the injured party's property, and a separate list of wild animals that are מועד.

phrases.english: And they answer: Ravina said:
It is missing words,
and this is what it teaches:
There are five that are innocuous.
And if they were warned, all five of them are forewarned;
and Tooth and Foot are forewarned from the start;
and this is 'the forewarned ox.'
And an ox that damages on the injured party's property —
is a dispute between Rabbi Tarfon and the Rabbis.
And there are other forewarned ones similar to these:
the wolf, and the lion, the bear,
and the leopard, and the bardelas, and the snake.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Filling in missing words in the משנה (חסורי מחסרא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's 'five מועדים' is a complete list of every animal that is מועד.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Five מועדים' means only the five acts that become מועד after warnings. The wild animals are a separate, added group.

steps.title: Crouching on vessels: large versus small
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's words 'not for crouching.' רבי אלעזר says this only applies to large vessels, because crouching on small vessels is normal for an animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And not for crouching.' רבי אלעזר said: They taught this only about large vessels. But small vessels — that is its normal way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to a new phrase in the משנה, 'not for crouching.' רבי אלעזר explains when it applies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says an animal is not automatically מועד for crouching on things. רבי אלעזר limits this to large vessels, since crouching on them is unusual and acts like goring. Crouching on small vessels is normal animal behavior, so it is treated like ordinary walking damage, which is מועד from the start.

keyTerms.meaning: To crouch or lie down (on things)

steps.confusionAlert: רבי אלעזר is not arguing with the משנה. He is narrowing it: 'not מועד for crouching' only applies to large vessels.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a key test throughout this פרק: damage from an animal's normal behavior is treated as מועד from the start, while unusual behavior starts as תם.

phrases.english: 'And not for crouching.'
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה, which says an ox is not considered מועד for crouching on things.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
They taught this only about large vessels,
but small vessels — that is its normal way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: explaining another phrase from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה's rule that an animal is not מועד for crouching applies only to large vessels. Crouching on small vessels is normal behavior, so the animal is מועד for it from the start.

steps.title: A ברייתא seems to support רבי אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that a ברייתא, which says an animal is מועד to crush vessels, supports רבי אלעזר's split between small and large vessels.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say a ברייתא supports him: 'An animal is מועד to walk in its normal way, and to break and crush a person, an animal, and vessels.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible proof for רבי אלעזר from a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says crushing vessels is normal for an animal, while the משנה says crouching on vessels is not normal. The two only fit together if, like רבי אלעזר, the ברייתא means small vessels and the משנה means large ones.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us say this supports him (a suggested proof, which often gets rejected)
Considered forewarned, so the owner pays full damage

phrases.english: Let us say this supports him:
phrases.notes: 'Him' is רבי אלעזר from the step before.

phrases.english: An animal is forewarned to walk in its normal way,
and to break and to crush

phrases.aramaic: אֶת הָאָדָם וְאֶת הַבְּהֵמָה וְאֶת הַכֵּלִים.
phrases.english: a person, and an animal, and vessels.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to prove רבי אלעזר's statement from step 12.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אלעזר's rule that crouching on small vessels is normal.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא saying an animal is מועד to crush vessels.

steps.title: The proof is rejected: crushing from the side
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא may be talking about an animal pushing vessels from the side, not crouching on them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps it means from the side.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the proof from the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the animal crushed the vessels by pushing them from the side as it walked, that is normal walking, not crouching. So the ברייתא says nothing about crouching, and it does not prove רבי אלעזר's split.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps (used to show another way to read a source)

phrases.english: Perhaps it is from the side.
phrases.notes: He means the animal pushed the vessels from the side while walking, instead of crouching on top of them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof offered in step 13.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof is rejected; רבי אלעזר's statement still stands.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא can be read as crushing from the side, not crouching.

steps.title: Second version: even small vessels are not normal for crouching
steps.stepSummary: In another version, רבי אלעזר says the opposite: crouching on small vessels is also not normal.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: רבי אלעזר said, Do not say that only large vessels are not normal, but small vessels are normal. Rather, even small vessels are also not normal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different version of רבי אלעזר's teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, crouching on small vessels was normal, so the owner pays full damage. In this version, crouching on any vessel, small or large, is not normal, so the משנה's rule covers all vessels.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new argument between two Rabbis. It is two reports of what רבי אלעזר himself said, and they say opposite things about small vessels.

phrases.english: There are those who say,
Rabbi Elazar said:
Do not say that large vessels
are what is not its normal way,
but small vessels are its normal way;
rather, even small vessels
are also not its normal way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an opposite version of רבי אלעזר's statement in step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Crouching on vessels of any size is not normal for an animal, so the animal is not מועד for it.

steps.title: The ברייתא about crushing vessels challenges the second version
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the second version using the ברייתא that says an animal is מועד to crush vessels.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged him: 'And to crush a person, an animal, and vessels!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the second version of רבי אלעזר using the same ברייתא from before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says crushing vessels is normal for an animal. In the second version, רבי אלעזר says crouching on even small vessels is not normal, so the ברייתא seems to go against him.

keyTerms.meaning: They raised a challenge (usually from a ברייתא or משנה)

phrases.english: They raised an objection:

phrases.aramaic: וּלְמַעֵךְ אֶת הָאָדָם וְאֶת הַבְּהֵמָה וְאֶת הַכֵּלִים!
phrases.english: And to crush a person, and an animal, and vessels!
phrases.notes: This is the same ברייתא from step 13. Now it is used to attack רבי אלעזר instead of to support him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the second version given in step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: The second version of רבי אלעזר: even small vessels are not normal for crouching.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא calls crushing vessels normal, which seems to contradict the claim that crouching on any vessel is not normal.

steps.title: The ברייתא may be talking about pushing from the side
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר answers the challenge to his second version: the ברייתא may mean the animal crushed vessels by pushing them from the side, not by crouching on them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: Perhaps the ברייתא is talking about crushing from the side.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from Step 16. The ברייתא that says an animal is מועד to crush vessels may be talking about side-pushing, not crouching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the second version, רבי אלעזר holds that crouching on any vessel, even a small one, is not normal. The ברייתא seemed to say crushing vessels is normal. By reading the ברייתא as side-pushing, he removes the conflict, so crouching stays abnormal for all vessels.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
Perhaps it is from the side.
phrases.notes: He means the animal pushed the vessels sideways, for example against a wall, while walking. It did not sit down on them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רבי אלעזר דלמא מן הצד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge raised in Step 16 against the second version.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the case in the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא says crushing vessels, even by crouching, is normal behavior.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא may be talking only about side-pushing, so crouching on any vessel can still be abnormal.

steps.title: A third version: the משנה and the ברייתא seem to contradict each other
steps.stepSummary: Some present the issue as a contradiction. The משנה says an animal is not מועד for crouching, but a ברייתא says it is מועד to crush people, animals, and vessels.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some raise this as a contradiction: We learned in the משנה, 'and not for crouching.' But a ברייתא teaches: 'and to crush a person, an animal, and vessels'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another way the same discussion was presented. Here it is a direct contradiction between two sources, not a question about רבי אלעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה treats crouching as abnormal, so the animal is not מועד for it. The ברייתא treats crushing as normal, so the animal is מועד from the start. Crushing usually happens by crouching, so the two sources seem to clash.

keyTerms.meaning: Some raise it as a contradiction
To crouch or lie down on something

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new topic. It is the same crouching discussion from Steps 12–17, told a different way.

phrases.english: There are those who raise it as a contradiction:
We learned in the משנה: 'and not for crouching.'
But isn't it taught in a ברייתא: 'and to crush'

phrases.aramaic: אֶת הָאָדָם וְאֶת הַבְּהֵמָה וְאֶת הַכֵּלִים!
phrases.english: a person, an animal, and vessels!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents the same crouching issue again, this time as a contradiction between sources.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that an animal is not מועד for crouching
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says an animal is מועד to crush vessels, which suggests crouching on them is normal behavior.

steps.title: Large vessels versus small vessels
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר resolves the contradiction. The משנה is about large vessels, and the ברייתא is about small vessels.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: It is not difficult. Here it is about large vessels, and there it is about small vessels.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר settles the contradiction from Step 18 by saying each source is talking about a different size of vessel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Crouching on large vessels is abnormal, so the משנה says the animal is not מועד. Crouching on small vessels is normal, so the ברייתא says the animal is מועד. This matches רבי אלעזר's first version in Step 12.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; there is no contradiction
Here... there; one source is about this case, the other about that case

steps.whatToRemember: In this version, crouching on large vessels is unusual behavior, while crouching on small vessels is normal behavior for an animal.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said: It is not difficult;
here it is about large vessels,
phrases.notes: 'Here' means the משנה, which says the animal is not מועד for crouching.

phrases.english: there it is about small vessels.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רבי אלעזר לא קשיא כאן בפכין גדולים כאן בפכין קטנים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in Step 18.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה and the ברייתא disagree about whether crushing vessels is normal.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each source is about a different size of vessel, so they do not disagree.

steps.title: What is a ברדלס?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to the משנה's list of wild animals that are מועד from the start and asks what a ברדלס is.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'The wolf and the lion, etc.' What is a ברדלס?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It quotes the משנה's list of dangerous animals and asks what one unclear animal name means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists animals that are מועד even if they never caused damage before. One of them, the ברדלס, is an unfamiliar word. The גמרא asks for a definition so we know which animal the rule covers.

keyTerms.meaning: Etc.; the rest of the quote
A wild animal listed in the משנה; its identity is being asked

phrases.english: 'The wolf and the lion, etc.'
What is a ברדלס?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new line of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identity of the animal called ברדלס

steps.title: רב יהודה says ברדלס is a נפרזא
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה answers that a ברדלס is a נפרזא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: It is a נפרזא.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה answers the question from Step 20 by giving another name for the ברדלס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He explains the משנה's word with a name that was familiar in his time. As the next step shows, that name still needs explaining.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said: A נפרזא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in Step 20.

steps.title: רב יוסף says נפרזא is an אפא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what a נפרזא is, and רב יוסף answers that it is an אפא.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is a נפרזא? רב יוסף said: An אפא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a follow-up question about רב יהודה's word, and רב יוסף explains it. This sets up the challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now we have a chain: ברדלס = נפרזא = אפא. This identification is the target of the coming challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: Another name for the נפרזא, and so for the ברדלס

phrases.english: What is a נפרזא?
Rav Yosef said: An אפא.

steps.triggerLanguage: מאי נפרזא אמר רב יוסף אפא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for and gives a definition of רב יהודה's answer.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A נפרזא is an אפא, so the ברדלס is an אפא.

steps.title: Challenge: רב יוסף also says the צבוע is an אפא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges using a ברייתא. רבי מאיר adds the צבוע to the משנה's list, and רב יוסף says the צבוע is an אפא. If the אפא is the ברדלס, it is already in the list.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: רבי מאיר says, also the צבוע. רבי אלעזר says, also the snake. And רב יוסף said: The צבוע is the אפא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a challenge against identifying the ברדלס as an אפא, using a ברייתא and another statement of רב יוסף.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר says 'also the צבוע,' meaning it is an addition to the משנה's list. But רב יוסף says the צבוע is the אפא, and in Step 22 the אפא was the ברדלס, which the משנה already lists. So how can the צבוע be an addition?

keyTerms.meaning: They raised an objection, usually from a ברייתא

phrases.english: They raised an objection: Rabbi Meir says:
Also the hyena.
Rabbi Elazar says: Also the snake.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: צָבוֹעַ זוֹ אַפָּא!
phrases.english: And Rav Yosef said: The hyena is the אפא!

steps.triggerLanguage: מיתיבי רבי מאיר אומר אף הצבוע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the identification of the ברדלס as an אפא given in Step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's identification of the ברדלס (נפרזא) as an אפא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב יוסף says the צבוע is the אפא, and רבי מאיר treats the צבוע as an addition to the list. If the אפא were the ברדלס, the צבוע would already be in the משנה.

steps.title: Male hyena versus female hyena
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא, where רבי מאיר adds the צבוע, means the male hyena. The משנה's ברדלס means the female hyena.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not a problem. Here (the ברייתא) is talking about a male hyena, and there (the משנה) is talking about a female hyena.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 23. It does this by splitting the hyena into two kinds, male and female.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question was: if the אפא, which is the ברדלס, is the צבוע, then the צבוע is already in the משנה's list. The answer is that the משנה's ברדלס is the female hyena. רבי מאיר adds the male hyena, which the משנה did not list. So his addition is not a repeat.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not a problem; a standard way to open an answer

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
here it is speaking of a male hyena,
phrases.notes: "Here" means the ברייתא where רבי מאיר adds the צבוע.

phrases.english: there it is speaking of a female hyena.
phrases.notes: "There" means the משנה, whose ברדלס is the female hyena.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא, כָּאן בְּצָבוֹעַ זָכָר, כָּאן בְּצָבוֹעַ נְקִיבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 23
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the case: two different kinds of the same animal
steps.terutzHavaAmina: צבוע and ברדלס look like one animal, so רבי מאיר's addition seems to repeat the משנה
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה lists the female hyena, and רבי מאיר adds the male hyena

steps.title: A ברייתא showing the male hyena is different
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא describes how a male hyena changes into other creatures over seven-year cycles. This shows that the male is treated separately from the female. The ברייתא also says a person's spine becomes a snake, but only if he did not bow at מודים.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: a male hyena becomes a bat after seven years. That bat becomes a different kind of bat after seven years. That becomes a thistle after seven years. The thistle becomes a briar after seven years. The briar becomes a שד (demon) after seven years. A person's spine becomes a snake seven years after he dies. This applies only to someone who did not bow at מודים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to support its answer that a male hyena is different from a female hyena.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא describes changes that happen only to the male hyena. So the male really is its own separate creature in the eyes of חז"ל. That makes it reasonable for רבי מאיר to list it apart from the female. The line about the spine is a related teaching in the same ברייתא, and the גמרא limits it to one who did not bow at מודים.

keyTerms.meaning: The blessing of thanks in the שמונה עשרה, where we bow

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא is quoted mainly for its first words, "a male hyena." They show the male is treated as its own creature. Don't get lost in the chain of changes. The main point is just that male and female are different.

phrases.english: As it is taught in a ברייתא:
A male hyena, after seven years,
becomes a bat;

phrases.aramaic: עֲטַלֵּף לְאַחַר שֶׁבַע שָׁנִים נַעֲשֶׂה עַרְפָּד,
phrases.english: the bat, after seven years, becomes another kind of bat;

phrases.aramaic: עַרְפָּד לְאַחַר שֶׁבַע שָׁנִים נַעֲשֶׂה קִימּוֹשׂ,
phrases.english: that bat, after seven years, becomes a thistle;

phrases.aramaic: קִימּוֹשׂ לְאַחַר שֶׁבַע שָׁנִים נַעֲשֶׂה חוֹחַ,
phrases.english: the thistle, after seven years, becomes a briar;

phrases.aramaic: חוֹחַ לְאַחַר שֶׁבַע שָׁנִים נַעֲשֶׂה שֵׁד.
phrases.english: the briar, after seven years, becomes a demon.
A person's spine,
after seven years, becomes a snake.
phrases.notes: Seven years after the person dies.

phrases.english: And this applies only
where he did not bow at "מודים".
phrases.notes: מודים is the thank-you blessing in שמונה עשרה, where we bow.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: צָבוֹעַ זָכָר לְאַחַר שֶׁבַע שָׁנִים נַעֲשֶׂה עֲטַלֵּף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings support for the answer given in Step 24
steps.raayaObject: That the male hyena is a creature distinct from the female
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא describing the changes of the male hyena

steps.title: Quoting רבי מאיר's addition again
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to quote the ברייתא's line again: רבי מאיר says the צבוע is also included. It does this to start a new discussion of that line.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: רבי מאיר says, also the hyena.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It quotes רבי מאיר's line again so it can look at it more closely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "אמר מר" is the way the גמרא goes back to an earlier source to examine it. Nothing new is ruled here yet. This step just opens a new line of analysis about the צבוע.

keyTerms.meaning: The Master said; the גמרא quotes an earlier source again in order to discuss it

phrases.english: The Master said:
Rabbi Meir says: also the hyena.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר, רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: אַף הַצָּבוֹעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the ברייתא from Step 23 to begin a new discussion
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר adds the hyena to the animals that are מועד from the start
